newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate steady on fresh bids.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate steady on fresh bids.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to as low as 7.7 percent but firmed back to 8.2 percent on fresh bids, dealers said on Tuesday.
The overnight traded between 7.5 and 8.2 percent on Monday.

"It will continue to hover around the 8.0 percent level," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "Bank Negara is lending but only to help ease market tightness. There's no excess liquidity in the market at the moment."
But the overnight rate should come off slightly on Friday when there will be a maturity of Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit, dealers said.
In the morning, interbank rates were slightly lower as Bank Negara continued to lend one-month money through an agent bank.
One-month money was at 8.0 percent against 8.3 percent on Monday, while the three-month rate was at 8.0/1 percent against 8.0/3 percent.
One-week money was steady at 7.9/8.3 percent.
Dealers said they expected one- and three-month rates to come down to around 7.5 percent in the near term amid growing perception that the authorities want to see lower interest rates.

In a move to help control interest rates more effectively, Bank Negara announced on Sunday that local banks would have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday.
On Friday, Bank Negara had asked banks to hold their base lending rates steady despite the recent surge in interbank rates.

Dealers said they heard that finance companies were being asked by Bank Negara not to bid in the market in order to keep rates down. In return, the firms can directly approach the central bank for funds.
Finance companies are considered higher risk borrowers in the market and have to bid at higher rates.
No confirmation was available from Bank Negara, which does not normally comment on its open market operations.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were little changed in thin activity after posting sharp gains on Monday.
At 0815 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was unchanged at 92.40, or an implied yield of 7.60 percent.
The December contract was down two points to 92.61, or 7.39 percent.
